svg.data-integrated-interfaces: 16 x 1GE SFP, 24 x 1/10GE SFP/SFP+, 2 x 100GE QSFP28
svg.data-port-modes-sfp: 1GbE only - data sheet Table 2, "16x1 GE", and the install guide, "16 ports that support 1 GbE (using SFP)". Cisco publishes no per-optic list for this chassis
svg.data-port-modes-sfp-plus: 1GbE or 10GbE dual-rate - install guide, "24 ports that support 1 GbE (using SFP) or 10 GbE (using SFP+)", with the note that 1 GE copper transceivers work from IOS-XR 7.0.1 at 1 GE only, and that 10 and 100 Mbps are not supported
svg.data-port-modes-qsfp28: 100GbE - data sheet Table 2, "2x100 GE". Figure 121 numbers them 20 and 21
svg.data-power-cord-family: Saf-D-Grid: CAB-AC-16A-SG-* at 16 A 250 VAC, CAB-AC-20A-SG-US/US1 at 20 A 110/125 VAC
svg.data-operating-temp: 5 to 40 C (41 to 104 F) nominal, -5 to 55 C short-term
svg.data-operating-humidity: 10 to 85 percent nominal, 5 to 90 percent short-term
svg.data-timing: 2 x BITS/J.211 SYNC RJ-45, IEEE 1588 service LAN and ToD RJ-45, 10 MHz and 1 PPS SMB
svg.data-nebs: designed to meet SR-3580 NEBS Criteria Level 3 and GR-1089-CORE NEBS EMC and Safety

Cisco ASR 9901 Router and Cisco ASR 9001 Router is 3.47 inches (8.8 cm)\", which is 88.14 - and note that one sentence covers two chassis, and that 3.47 in is the ASR 9001's own data sheet figure. THE DATA SHEET IS CARRIED AND THE STENCIL IS WHY. THE WINDOW STANDS ON END, and that is settled. It was two drawings agreeing, which is one drawing counted twice - the stencil master and Figure 12's line art, both portrait, both hatched with diagonals, either of which could have been a draughting symbol for \"display\". It is not a symbol: photographs of three real units show a light rounded bezel left of the CISCO wordmark with a dark portrait window in it, and the sharpest resolves the DIAMOND LATTICE the drawings were tracing. So Cisco's \"one row of four characters\" reads TURNED. WHICH WAY IT TURNS IS IN NOTHING. Up or down, no document says. Fourteen resale listings for this chassis were opened and every unit photographed is POWERED OFF, so not one of them reads the matrix. Searched both, plus the data sheet, for each legend by name. SO THE COLOURS ARE READ OFF THE NAMES - red for CRIT, amber for MAJ and MIN, green for SSD, GPS, SYNC and INPUT OK - and every one of the nine says so in its own description rather than leaving the reading to be inferred from the fact that a colour is written down.","reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["alarms"],"wanted":"a Cisco LED table for the ASR 9901 front panel.","what":"nine-alarm-lamps-have-no-state-table"},{"blocks":[],"note":"THE TOP, BOTTOM AND TWO SIDES ARE SIZED AND NOT DRAWN, and each carries an `empty:` sentence saying where the search ran. Cisco's ordering tables give them different part numbers, ASR-9901-FAN and ASR-9902-FAN, and that is the only reason this library holds two contracts. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT is a photograph of either tray's label, or the two in one hand. Table 11 of the install guide, \"AC-Input Power Cord Options for Cisco ASR 9901 Router\", lists sixteen cords and every one is a CAB-AC-*-SG-* - sixteen amps at 250 VAC across Europe, the UK, Japan, Australia, India and the rest, and CAB-AC-20A-SG-US and -US1 at twenty amps for North America. SG is Cisco's Saf-D-Grid, and the master draws that profile rather than a C14: a shrouded rectangular body with a stepped keyway. THE RATING IS WHY. 1600 W off a 90 V low line is nearly eighteen amps, which is past what a C14 carries, so the connector is not a detail somebody chose freely. THE PART NOW EXISTS AND THE MODULE COMPOSES IT. std/saf-d-grid@1 carries Anderson Power Products' own panel cutout - 26.80 x 19.90 mm, corners R2.5 max, off APP drawing 115171S1 rev 12 - and cisco/a9k-1600w-ac@1 places it `rotate: 90` because this module mounts the receptacle upright. The gap this file used to carry for it is closed. AND THE TWO SOURCES AGREE WITHOUT EVER HAVING BEEN COMPARED. This chassis's rear master draws the module's aperture 19.98 x 26.51 mm at a scale set by the body width alone; Anderson's cutout turned a quarter turn is 19.90 x 26.80 - 0.4 percent across and 1.1 percent down, between two documents that share no author, no units convention and no measurement, and neither of which was an input to the other."},"air-filter":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"NOT DRAWN. The ASR 9901 ordering table in c78-740540 lists no filter PID - unlike the ASR 9902 and ASR 9903, which both have one - and the install guide's air-filter chapter covers the 9001, 9902 and 9903 and not this chassis. So there is nothing to draw and nothing to record as missing. ASR-9901-CAB-MGMT is left out for the reason the modelling guide gives for cable management generally: it is not a panel fact."},"chassis":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"datasheet - Table 2 of c78-740540: height 3.43 in. (8.7 cm), width 17.32 in. (44 cm), depth 23.62 in. (60 cm); chassis weight 47.62 lb (21.6 kg), or 55.97 lb (25.4 kg) fully configured with 2 power modules and 3 fan trays. The inch figures are carried because the centimetre ones beside them are rounded to two significant figures: 3.43 in is 87.12 mm, 17.32 in is 439.93, 23.62 in is 599.95. `chassis.weight-kg` is the FULLY CONFIGURED 25.4, because that is what the other chassis in this family carry and what a rack calculation wants; the bare 21.6 is in attrs beside it. THE HEIGHT DISAGREES WITH THE INSTALL GUIDE and the disagreement is recorded as a gap rather than averaged. The guide says \"Height of the ... Cisco ASR 9901 Router and Cisco ASR 9001 Router is 3.47 inches (8.8 cm)\" - one sentence covering two chassis, and 3.47 in is the ASR 9001's own data sheet figure. The stencil settles it: the REAR master's ink is 550.64 art units tall and its shape box reads 87.38 mm, so at the width-anchored scale the body comes out 87.11 mm against the data sheet's 87.12. Two independent readings agreeing to a hundredth of a millimetre beat one sentence that looks like a sibling's number reused. WIDTH IS THE BODY: 17.32 in is not the 19 in rack face, so L43 has nothing to catch, and the install guide's mounting section agrees from the other side - \"the usable aperture ... must be at least 17.75 inches (45.09 cm) for the Cisco ASR 9901 Router\"."},"cooling":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"datasheet - \"Redundancy: Power supply and Fan redundancy\" and \"Air flow: Front to Back\", and the install guide adds the count: \"Cisco ASR 9901 Router has three fan trays.\" THE REDUNDANCY RATIO IS NOT PUBLISHED AND IS NOT SUPPLIED. The `fan-trays` group carries a note and no `redundancy`, and L69 warns that this chassis does not say how many fans it can lose - the same ruling the ASR 9902 and ASR 9903 carry, and edgecore/csr310 before them. THE TRAY NUMBERING RUNS RIGHT TO LEFT. The master prints FAN 2 on the leftmost tray, FAN 1 in the middle and FAN 0 on the right, which is the opposite of the power modules two rows over, where PM1 is left of PM0. Both are carried as printed."},"face-check":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"done BEFORE measuring, because Cisco's master filenames name the wrong faces on the ASR 9910. No swap here. \"ASR-9901 Front\" carries the forty-two numbered ports, the GRP 0 to GRP 5 group labels, the timing and management jacks, the nine alarm lamps, the LED matrix and the CISCO / ASR9901 branding, and matches Figure 5 of the install guide, \"Front Panel of the Cisco ASR 9901 Router\", feature for feature. \"ASR-9901 Rear\" carries three fan trays and two power modules and matches Figure 6."},"grounding":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"install guide for what it is, master for where. Figure 76, \"NEBS Bonding and Grounding Points on the Cisco ASR 9901 Router\". The rear master draws a two-hole lug landing on the panel above the power modules, holes 15.96 mm apart on centres, with an IEC 60417-5019 earth mark beside it. cisco/a9k-ground-pad@1 carries a 15.3 mm two-hole pitch, which covers it to within 0.66 mm, and it is placed unrotated because the lug lies flat."},"lamps":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing for the count and the arrangement, guide for the count again. Nine lamps in a three-by-three grid at the right of the control row, printed SSD, FAN FLT and GPS across the top, CRIT, MAJ and MIN across the middle, and RSP FAIL, LC STAT / INPUT OK and SYNC across the bottom. Figure 12's callout 8 says \"Nine discrete LED indicators\", which is the same nine. THE MIDDLE LAMP OF THE BOTTOM ROW CARRIES TWO LEGENDS, LC STAT above INPUT OK, and the master draws one lens for them. It is modelled as one lamp with both words in its description rather than as two, because two lenses is not what the drawing shows and nine is what the guide counts. THE POSITIONS ARE READ OFF A 2x RENDER BY EYE. The lamps are drawn as stroked circles with no fill, which the shape parser does not carry - the same situation cisco/a99-rp-f@1 records for its own nine. The LEGENDS are extracted text and their positions are exact; the lens centres are a consistent 2.2 mm left of their legend. NO STATE TABLE FOR THESE NINE IS IN THE INTAKE. The guide's RP Front Panel Indicators section covers the ASR 9001's cluster and the LED matrix, and Table 21 covers line cards, supplies and fan trays. So each lamp carries the colours its name implies - red for CRIT, amber for MAJ and MIN, green for SSD, GPS, SYNC and INPUT OK - and that is a READING of the names, flagged here rather than presented as sourced."},"led-matrix":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"install guide for what it is, master for where. The LED matrix shows one row of four characters. It comes alive when the CPU powers on, shows the stages of the boot and then runtime information in normal operation, and shows error messages when there are CAN Bus Controller problems. Table 25 and Table 26 list the twenty-eight readings, and cisco/led-matrix-4@1 carries them. IT IS A PLACED PART NOW AND NOT PANEL DECOR. It was two decor rectangles until `class: display` learned to say how many characters it shows and what they can read; the part carries the same two rectangles, measured the same way, and the model can now be asked what the display says. Its box is read off a 2x render by eye, because the bezel is a stroked rounded rectangle the parser does not carry. NO CUTOUT IS PUNCHED FOR IT. The bezel lands on the metal and the window is the aperture, but nothing in the intake dimensions that aperture apart from the drawn window, and L63 wants a cutout to restate a component's own opening exactly. So the part draws its window and the panel declares no hole, which is what every other display in this library does."},"port-groups":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing - the twenty-four dual-rate ports are printed GRP 0 to GRP 5, six labels over six pairs of columns, four ports to a group: GRP 0 over ports 8 to 11, GRP 1 over 12 to 15, GRP 2 over 16 to 19, GRP 3 over 22 to 25, GRP 4 over 26 to 29 and GRP 5 over 30 to 33. NO DOCUMENT IN THE INTAKE SAYS WHAT A GRP IS on this chassis - the configuration guide's slice mechanism is written for the ASR 9902 and the PECs and names no groups here - so the labels are carried as printed and nothing is claimed about what they constrain. The rate legends under the blocks are the master's own: 1GE, 10/1GE, 100GE, 10/1GE, 1GE."},"ports":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"FORTY-TWO PORTS, AND THE THREE SOURCES AGREE. Table 2 of c78-740540 gives \"Integrated interfaces: 16x1 GE, 24x 1/10 GE, 2x100 GE\". The install guide spells the same thing out: the ASR 9901 has an integrated route processor (RP) and 42 fixed ports, among them 24 that take 1 GbE (SFP) or 10 GbE (SFP+) and 16 that take 1 GbE (SFP), plus two QSFP28. And Figure 121, \"Cisco ASR 9901 Fixed Ports\", numbers them: \"1 SFP ports (0-7), 2 SFP/SFP+ ports (8-19), 3 QSFP28 ports (20-21), 4 SFP/SFP+ ports (22-33), 5 SFP ports (34-41)\". THE MASTER PRINTS ALL FORTY-TWO NUMERALS and they match Figure 121 block for block: 0 to 7 over the left four columns, 8 to 19 over the next six, 20 and 21 on the stacked 100GE cage, 22 to 33 over the next six and 34 to 41 over the last four. Even numbers on the top row throughout. THE DUAL-RATE PORTS COME WITH A CAVEAT THE GUIDE PRINTS ITSELF: from Cisco IOS-XR Software Release 7.0.1 the ASR 9901 supports 1 GE copper transceivers in its dual-rate ports, at the 1 GE rate only; 10 Mbps and 100 Mbps are not supported."},"power":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"datasheet - Table 2 of c78-740540: \"Power supply part number: A9K-1600W-AC, A9K-1600W-DC\", \"Power inputs: Worldwide ranging AC (90-265V; 50-60 Hz), Worldwide ranging DC (-40V to -72V)\", \"Power consumption: 850 watts typical, 1100 watts maximum\", and \"Redundancy: Power supply and Fan redundancy\". THESE ARE NOT THE ASR 9902'S SUPPLIES. That chassis takes PWR-1.6KW-AC and -DC; this one takes A9K-1600W-AC and -DC, and the master draws a 71.21 x 39.21 mm module against the other's 74.94 x 40.91. Same wattage, different part, different envelope. THE CHASSIS FIGURE IS THE VENDOR'S AND IS NOT RECONCILED against the module total. 850 W typical and 1100 W maximum are what the box draws; 2 x 1600 W is what the supplies can give."},"power-switch":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing AND install guide. The master draws a recessed slider at the left of the control row under a yellow tag reading ATTENTION / ON-OFF FOR ENTIRE SHELF, and Figure 156, \"Power Switch on the Cisco ASR 9901\", names it. The step it illustrates is the same one the ASR 9902 gets: \"Set the power switch to the ON position.\" IT IS SEATED RATHER THAN PAINTED, using common/power-switch-slide@1 - the part the ASR 9902 introduced - because a switch is a thing a viewer should be able to click. THE TAG WORDING IS THE CHASSIS'S OWN and is printed here rather than taken from the part: this chassis says ON-OFF FOR ENTIRE SHELF where the ASR 9902 says ON-OFF, and the component's own tag carries the shorter wording. THERE IS NO SEPARATE POWER-STATUS LAMP BESIDE IT on this chassis. The ASR 9902 has one; here the master draws none, and the nine-lamp cluster carries INPUT OK instead."},"sources":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"the Cisco ASR 9901 Router Data Sheet (c78-740540, 2021); the Cisco ASR 9000 Series Fixed-Port Routers Hardware Installation Guide (b-asr9001-hardware-installation-guide.pdf, last modified 2021-07-30, which despite its filename covers the 9001, 9901, 9902 and 9903); and Cisco's own Visio stencil Routers-Cisco_ASR_9000, masters \"ASR-9901 Front\" and \"ASR-9901 Rear\"."},"stencil-calibration":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"THE TWO MASTERS USE DIFFERENT CONVENTIONS, as they do on the ASR 9902: \"ASR-9901 Front\" reads 482.60 x 88.90 mm - the 19 in rack face by the 2 RU ALLOCATION - and \"ASR-9901 Rear\" reads 482.60 x 87.38, the rack face by the chassis as built. Each is calibrated on its own. THE BODY BOX IS NOT THE INK BOX ON THE FRONT, and getting that wrong is a 1.7 percent error in y. The front master's ink runs 561.30 units tall because the bezel draws a lip above and below the chassis; the RACK EAR beside it runs 6.00 to 556.55, and that 550.55-unit span is the body. Set to 87.12 mm it gives ky 0.158242 against kx 0.158210 from the 2780.68-unit body width at 439.93 mm - 0.02 percent apart, which is this stencil's best calibration yet. The rear needs no such care: its body ink is 550.64 units and comes out 0.00 percent apart. THE RULER INSIDE THE ARTWORK CONFIRMS BOTH. The twenty SFP-class cage columns across the four port blocks sit on a measured 14.24 mm pitch, constant to 0.01 over nineteen consecutive gaps, against SFF-8433's 14.25 for a ganged SFP assembly - 0.07 percent, on a dimension that was never an input. The 100GE bores then measure 18.95 x 8.96 mm against std/qsfp-ganged's 18.5 x 9.58, and the nine RJ-45 jacks 12.66 x 10.76 against std/rj45-ganged's 12.7 x 11.0."},"the-1588-jack-is-ethernet-doing-a-timing-job":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"L76 REPORTS THIS ONE AND IT IS RIGHT TO, so here is the reading rather than a silenced warning. The IEEE 1588 service LAN jack sits in the `timing` group, because what it is FOR is telling this router the time - and it is seated as common/rj45-ganged-eth@1, the lamped Ethernet part, because what it IS is an Ethernet port. The master draws LINK and ACT beside it, and Table 4 of the same install guide describes the equivalent jack on the ASR 9001 as \"Service LAN Port (IEEE 1588) | RJ45 | A 10/100Mbps Ethernet Port for IEEE1588 Grand Master Connection through CAT5 cable\". docs/rj45-family-design.md sorts jacks by job and this one has two, so whichever part it takes, one of the two rules disagrees. The lamped part is carried because the lamps are drawn on the hardware; taking std/rj45-ganged to quiet the rule would remove two lamps the device has."}},"references":[{"sha256":"a3a57e6e3e66efd22c1e506ca7a742bc62784dd07b0fb9a9d0274fa7726d0d31","title":"Cisco ASR 9901 Router Data Sheet (c78-740540, 2021)"},{"sha256":"8b539355306e5bd2cfd9293a07dfe3acc95cb6aa95435537225b667901ac9d13","title":"Cisco ASR 9000 Series Fixed-Port Routers Hardware Installation Guide (2021-07-30)"}],"version":"0.3.2","views":{"bottom":{"empty":"the bottom carries the feet and the bracket landings and is photographed in no figure.
